questions.question: What freedom does a commercial bank have regarding interest rates on Resident Foreign Currency (RFC) account deposits?
questions.answer: A commercial bank has the freedom to determine interest rates on deposits accepted or renewed under the RFC Account Scheme, subject to its Board-approved comprehensive deposit interest rate policy.
questions.evidence: A bank shall have the freedom to determine interest on deposits of money accepted by it or renewed by it under the RFC Account Scheme, in accordance with the comprehensive policy on interest rate on deposits duly approved by the Board of Directors

questions.question: Who must approve the comprehensive policy on interest rates on deposits that governs RFC account interest rates at a commercial bank?
questions.answer: The comprehensive policy on interest rates on deposits must be approved by the Board of Directors or any Committee of the Board to which powers have been delegated.
questions.evidence: in accordance with the comprehensive policy on interest rate on deposits duly approved by the Board of Directors or any Committee of the Board to which powers have been delegated.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum interest rate a commercial bank can offer on RFC account deposits under these Directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph grants banks freedom to determine rates subject to a Board-approved policy but does not specify any maximum interest rate ceiling for RFC deposits.

questions.question: Which commercial banks are permitted to accept rupee deposits from non-residents under NRE and NRO accounts?
questions.answer: Only commercial banks that have been authorised under the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 by the Reserve Bank of India may accept such deposits.
questions.evidence: Rupee deposits of non-residents under NRE and NRO deposits shall be accepted only by those banks that are authorised under Foreign Exchange Management Act,1999 (FEMA) by Reserve Bank of India from time to time.

questions.question: What categories of non-resident rupee deposits does this rule cover?
questions.answer: The rule covers Non-Resident External (NRE) and Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) rupee deposits.
questions.evidence: Rupee deposits of non-residents under NRE and NRO deposits shall be accepted only by those banks that are authorised under Foreign Exchange Management Act,1999 (FEMA) by Reserve Bank of India from time to time.

unanswerable.question: How frequently does the Reserve Bank of India review or renew the FEMA authorisation for banks to accept NRE and NRO deposits?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states authorisation is granted 'from time to time' but does not specify any review frequency, renewal period, or deadline for such authorisations.

questions.question: What foreign currency funding sources are permitted for a commercial bank to extend pre-shipment credit in foreign currency (PCFC)?
questions.answer: A commercial bank may use foreign currency funds borrowed under FEMA Notification No. FEMA.3(R)/2018-RB dated December 17, 2018, and funds generated through buy-sell swaps in the domestic forex market.
questions.evidence: foreign currency funds borrowed in terms of Notification No. FEMA.3(R)/2018-RB dated December 17, 2018 as also foreign currency funds generated through buy-sell swaps in the domestic forex market

questions.question: What regulatory limit must a commercial bank observe when deploying foreign currency funds for PCFC?
questions.answer: The bank must adhere to the Aggregate Gap Limit (AGL) as specified in the Master Direction on Risk Management and Inter-Bank Dealings.
questions.evidence: subject to adherence to Aggregate Gap Limit (AGL) in terms of Master Direction - Risk Management and Inter-Bank Dealings

unanswerable.question: What is the specific Aggregate Gap Limit (AGL) percentage that a commercial bank must maintain for PCFC?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that PCFC must be subject to adherence to the Aggregate Gap Limit but does not specify the numerical limit; it refers to another Master Direction for those details.

questions.question: What must a commercial bank do when a guarantor fails to honor their commitment after it has been invoked?
questions.answer: The bank must report the guarantor's details to credit information companies as either a large defaulter or a wilful defaulter, depending on the case.
questions.evidence: A bank shall report to credit information companies the details of guarantors who have failed to honour the commitments thereunder when invoked, as large defaulters / wilful defaulters, as the case may be.

questions.question: Which reporting format must a commercial bank use when submitting details of guarantors who have defaulted on invoked commitments?
questions.answer: The bank must report the details as per Annex I and Annex II of the Directions.
questions.evidence: The details shall be reported as per Annex I and II.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days must a commercial bank report a guarantor who has failed to honor an invoked commitment to credit information companies?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any time limit or deadline for reporting such guarantors.

questions.question: What is the maximum cash amount a walk-in customer can use to obtain an at-par cheque from our urban co-operative bank?
questions.answer: Walk-in customers may obtain at-par cheques against cash only for amounts less than ₹50,000 per individual.
questions.evidence: for walk-in customers against cash for less than ₹50,000 per individual

questions.question: Are we required to cross all at-par cheques we issue as 'account payee' regardless of the amount?
questions.answer: Yes, every at-par cheque issued must be crossed 'account payee' irrespective of the amount involved.
questions.evidence: ensure that 'At par' cheques issued are crossed 'account payee' irrespective of the amount involved

unanswerable.question: Within how many days must our urban co-operative bank complete the periodic review of the at-par cheque facility arrangement with the commercial bank?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that such arrangements shall be reviewed to assess risks but does not specify any timeline, frequency, or deadline for conducting the review.
